## What you will do

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `learnr`, `fpp3`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## SES from scratch
```{r ses-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=14}
ses_levels <- function(y, alpha = 0.2) {
  n <- length(y)
  level <- numeric(n)
  ell <- y[1]
  level[1] <- ell
  for (t in 2:n) {
    ell <- alpha * y[t] + (1 - alpha) * ell
    level[t] <- ell
  }
  level
}
ses_levels(c(10, 12, 11, 13), 0.5)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("12", correct = TRUE),
  answer("10"),
  answer("13"),
  answer("11"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Level-shift demo
```{r shift-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
set.seed(1)
z <- c(rnorm(50, 10, 1), rnorm(50, 14, 1))
plot(z, type = "l")
lines(ses_levels(z, 0.1), col = "blue", lwd = 2)
lines(ses_levels(z, 0.8), col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

## fable SES vs SNAIVE
```{r fable-ses, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
library(fpp3)
train <- aus_production |> filter_index(. ~ "2005 Q4")
train |>
  model(SES = SES(Beer), SNaive = SNAIVE(Beer)) |>
  forecast(h = 8) |>
  autoplot(aus_production)
```

```{r q3}
question_text(

  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "SES has no seasonality; Beer does …",
  trim = TRUE
)
```
